title: Unpaid Interest and Fee Reserve in Operating Lines of Credit Shortfall Paydowns
content:
When the paydown that brings an Operating Lines of Credit line back within its borrowing base is figured, the lendable limit is reduced by a reserve for what the line already owes in billed interest and fees.

## Rule

The lendable limit is reduced by a reserve of:

- **the billed interest not yet paid plus the fees assessed on the line and not yet paid or waived**, when billed interest is unpaid and the due date of the line's latest interest bill has passed;
- **the unpaid fees alone**, when no billed interest is past due in that sense and fees are owed;
- **nothing**, when no billed interest is past due and no fee is owed.

## The quantities, from the line's transaction history

- **Billed interest not yet paid**: the interest billed on the line, plus interest payments returned unpaid, less interest payments, rounded to cents.
- **Fees not yet paid or waived**: the fees assessed on the line less fee payments and less fee waivers, rounded to cents.
- **Past due**: billed interest is unpaid and the due date of the bill with the latest due date is earlier than today; on that due date itself it has not yet passed.

## Combinations (hypothetical line)

| Billed interest unpaid | Latest bill's due date passed | Fees owed | Reserve |
|---|---|---|---|
| USD 4,000 | Yes | USD 500 | USD 4,500 |
| USD 4,000 | Yes | None | USD 4,000 |
| USD 4,000 | No — due today or later | USD 500 | USD 500 |
| None | — | USD 500 | USD 500 |
| None | — | None | Nothing |
| USD 4,000 | No | None | Nothing |

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A lendable limit of USD 1,400,000.00 with USD 4,000.00 of past-due billed interest and USD 500.00 of unpaid fees stands at USD 1,395,500.00 after the reserve.
